title: GPU capacity concierge notes and regional contingency sketch - Dec 04 2029
body:
Purpose:
Quick weekly capture from the capacity concierge sync (informal): roll-call of region signals, short contingency sketches for customer-facing Dedicated migrations, and a few experimental notes to carry into next sprint. This is intentionally concise — use as the single-source huddle note for on-call and concierge rotation this week.

Attendees:
- Aisha (owner)
- Rafael (concierge lead)
- Sofia (regional ops - EU/ME)
- Evan (edge capacity automation)
- Marta (SRE - incident liaison)
- Notes pulled into channel #gpu-capacity-concierge for asynchronous followups.

Agenda:
1) Fleet snapshot and immediate risks
2) Region-specific contingency sketches (short, executable)
3) Dedicated customer migrations / concierge ops items
4) Experiments / priming status and quick wins
5) Action items and owners

1) Fleet snapshot (Dec 04 morning window):
- Global usable pool: 64,200 vGPU-slots equivalent (weighted by instance class).
- Average 7d utilization: 78% global, 83% US-West peak window, 61% APAC off-peak.
- Spare headroom (operational target = 10%): current spare ~9%. On the edge relative to our SLA buffer for canaries.
- Observed preemptible eviction rate (7d) US-West: 1.9% (up from 0.6% last week) — correlates with cloud provider reclaim events on node group gpux-uw2-b.
- Latency SLO tail (p99 token latency) bump in EU-West for seqlen>2048: +25ms since config change on 11/30 (likely kernel selection mismatch on shuffled kernel set).

Interpretation: Utilization creeping into the no-margin zone for aggressive canaries. Preemptible churn is the largest single risk for predictable throughput this week.

2) Region contingency sketches (prioritized, short):
- US-West (primary risk):
  - Sketch: Gridcap fallback -> reduce batch-size cap on canaries by 20%, enable aggressive slot-shift to US-Central for non-latency-bound workloads.
  - Quick steps: toggle canary batch cap flag (ff-gc-canary-batch) -> ops-runbook step 3.1; notify concierge customers with migration windows.
  - Owner: Rafael; ETA: 4h to toggle + smoke tests.

- EU-West:
  - Sketch: Kernel-selection rollback window (revert kernel-set v12 -> v11 for models > 7B) while we test p99 edges.
  - Quick steps: roll 1 zone at a time, watch p99 for 2h, then roll remaining zones.
  - Owner: Sofia; ETA: 6h to roll first zone.

- APAC (opportunity window):
  - Sketch: Opportunistic backfill for Dedicated migration rehearsals (APAC nights show spare capacity).
  - Quick steps: schedule dry-run migration of customer D-302 next Tue 00:00-02:00 PT, add automated rollback threshold at 3% error rate.
  - Owner: Evan; Coordinated with Platform team.

3) Dedicated customer migration / concierge items:
- D-302 (media analytics) dry-run planned (see above). Primary goal: validate routing policy + KV cache warmup on target region.
- D-187 (financial services) requested hard SLA for Dec 12 rollout. We recommended a 3-phase approach: prewarm + staged traffic shift (5%, 25%, 70%). Concern: preemptible exposure in US-West needs mitigation before phase 1.
- Concierges will send short notice templates to customers by EOD 12/05 if we enable US-Central fallback. Template draft in #templates/dedicated-migration.

4) Experiments / priming status and quick wins:
- Prewarming agent experiment (eviction-aware): last-week run reduced cold-start tail by 18% for the sampled models. Next: extend to model size > 13B and measure token cost delta.
- KV-cache persistence test in APAC: partial success, checkpointing reduced recompute by ~12% but added 0.4% increase in transient CPU on host — need small tuning.
- Batching policy autotuner: early telemetry shows 7% cost improvement but increases p95 by ~10ms for low-latency routes. Proposal: enable for background routes, keep disabled for low-latency SLO tiers.
- Small quick wins: tweak node-scheduling affinity on gpux-uw2-b to co-locate lower-priority backfills with preemptible-friendly nodes.

5) Open questions / risks:
- If preemptible eviction rate >3% sustained in US-West, do we trigger automatic traffic shift for all canaries? (Decision pending)
- How do we communicate a rolling kernel rollback with product/console so customers see a single cohesive message? (P0 comms owner needed)
- Are there billing implications for customers if we shift them to higher-cost regions during contingency? Legal/pricing check requested.

Action items (owner / due):
- Rafael: flip ff-gc-canary-batch to -20% threshold and run smoke tests; report in channel (due 2029-12-04 16:00).
- Sofia: start EU-West kernel rollback scaffolding for zone-1 (due 2029-12-04 18:30) and capture p99 cadence.
- Evan: schedule D-302 dry-run in APAC dry-window and add rollback thresholds to orchestration job (due 2029-12-05 02:00).
- Marta: draft tentative comms for D-187 escalation plan and run by GTM/legal (due 2029-12-05 11:00).
- Aisha: open a short incident-runbook pull request capturing the toggle steps and runbook links (PR ref in linked_artifacts) (due 2029-12-05 09:00).

Notes to self / informal scribbles:
- We should add a simple safety check to routing policy: if global spare <8% and preemptible eviction >1.5% => decrease canary concurrency multiplier. Quick flag exists in routing config - but not wired into autoscaler yet.
- Consider a short-lived "concierge reserve" of 1k slots we only use for customer migrations to avoid repeated cold starts. Could be billed as a reserved staging pool (product discussion needed).
- Quick metric to add to console: "Gridcap factor" = (usable slots - reserved) / 7d peak demand; helps visualize headroom.

Decisions made during sync:
- No immediate mass-shift; prefer simmer strategies (batch cap + targeted rollbacks) this window.
- Proceed with D-302 dry-run in APAC.

Followups scheduled:
- Friday 09:00 sync to confirm US-West eviction rate and whether to escalate to traffic shift.
- Post-mortem if preemptible eviction >3% for 24h straight.

Appendix (links / quick refs):
- Fleet dashboard (internal): https://dash.redwood-internal/fleet/capacity
- Prewarming experiment notes: JIRA-PRIME-2034
- Runbook draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fleet-tooling/pull/562

If anything above looks off or you need a different cadence for the concierge rotation, ping me directly. This note will be updated after smoke tests and the EOD comms send.

-- Aisha
